family.tagline: A treehouse office with a Core on the desk.
family.story: Imani is a technical writer who rents a treehouse by the lake in Carrowmere. Her office is a desk in the sleeping nook, and her friend Jonah visits on weekends. Her clients' drafts sit on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Basil
companion.job: Opens Docmost in its own browser and files the draft Imani points to.
companion.limits: Files drafts only. Imani reviews every page.

popup.title: A parcel goes up the ladder
popup.body: The parcel waits at the foot of the ladder. Jonah, here for the weekend, hauls it up to the door and across to the desk.

popup.title: Imani reads the guide first
popup.body: Imani reads the quick-start guide first. Beside it: the Companion Core, a power cable and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Step one: plug it in
popup.body: Imani plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Step two: join it
popup.body: Imani joins the Core's own network from her phone. Jonah reads out the home Wi-Fi password, and she types it in.

popup.title: Step three: pick the apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Imani picks OpenClaw and adds Docmost, Logseq and VaultWarden. Then she walks away to make tea.

beats.capability: OpenClaw is an agent with its own browser and coding tools, running in its own sandbox, with iOS

popup.title: Basil answers, briefly
popup.body: Imani messages Basil, the agent she named. Basil answers in one dry line, and the Core is running.

say.speaker: imani
say.text: Hello, Imani. Basil here. Which page first?

beats.capability: Stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Saturday is film night
popup.body: Jellyfin plays Jonah's own film files on the wall TV while Imani takes the loveseat. The films stream from the Core.

beats.capability: Save articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service

popup.title: Saved articles, read by the fire
popup.body: By the fireplace, Imani reads the articles she bookmarked in Readeck. They sit on the Core, ready for the evening.

beats.capability: Plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: Sunday's lakeshore walk, planned
popup.body: Jonah sprawls on the loveseat and plans Sunday's lakeshore walk in Wanderer. The GPX route is saved on the Core.

beats.capability: Track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: A small pantry, fully listed
popup.body: The treehouse kitchen is small, so Imani tracks the pantry in Grocy. It lists what is on the shelf and builds the shopping list.

beats.capability: Split shared costs with housemates, family or friends and settle up with the fewest payments

popup.title: Who owes whom, settled
popup.body: Jonah and Imani split the weekend shop in Spliit. It shows who owes whom, so nobody has to do the sums.

beats.capability: A collaborative wiki for notes and documentation

popup.title: Basil files the draft
popup.body: Imani points Basil at a finished draft. Basil opens Docmost in its own browser and files the page. Imani reviews every page.

say.speaker: imani
say.text: Draft filed. Please review the page.

beats.capability: Write a private knowledge base and daily journal in plain Markdown files

popup.title: The outline starts in the journal
popup.body: Imani starts each client job in the daily journal in Logseq: an outline, three questions, one deadline. The notes are plain Markdown files on the Core.

beats.capability: Draw flowcharts, floor plans and network maps in the browser

popup.title: A flowchart for step four
popup.body: For a client's setup guide, Imani draws a flowchart in draw.io. The diagram is saved on the Core beside the draft.

beats.capability: Track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Hours, per client, in a report
popup.body: Imani tracks her hours per client in Kimai. Before she writes an invoice, she reads the report.

beats.capability: Chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Plain language, on a local model
popup.body: Imani asks the model in Open WebUI to restate a dense paragraph in plain language. The model runs on the Core. She keeps what reads well and rewrites the rest.

beats.capability: A PDF toolkit that runs in your browser

popup.title: The finished guide, one PDF
popup.body: Imani merges the finished guide and its diagrams into one PDF with BentoPDF. It runs in the browser, and nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: Store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Client logins, kept in a vault
popup.body: Imani keeps each client's logins in VaultWarden. It works with the Bitwarden apps, and the vault lives on the Core.

beats.capability: Read the sites you follow in one feed, on your own Core

popup.title: The morning feeds, in one place
popup.body: At the writing desk in the loft, Imani reads the sites she follows in FreshRSS. Her feed lives on the Core.

beats.capability: Read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: A novel before sleep
popup.body: In the tree bedroom, Imani reads a novel in Koodo Reader. Her highlights stay with the book, and the library lives on the Core.

beats.capability: Send a push notification to your phone from any script or automation with one request

popup.title: A buzz when the build ends
popup.body: Imani starts a long docs build and steps outside. A script sends a ntfy note to her phone when it ends.

beats.capability: Read Wikipedia and other reference sites offline

popup.title: Settling a wildflower argument
popup.body: Imani and Jonah disagree about a wildflower below the ladder. Kiwix settles it, from a copy of Wikipedia on the Core.

beats.capability: Stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

popup.title: A playlist for the deck
popup.body: Jonah queues his playlist on the deck. mStream streams it from the Core, and the lake does the rest.

popup.title: One desk, one ladder
popup.body: A treehouse on a lake, a desk in the sleeping nook and a friend on the weekends. The Keane household runs it all from one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your drafts, your clients' files and your build alerts can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one page in Docmost.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
The care note asks for no internet claims and nothing about being off the grid. The text says neither. The only internet mention is the standard ftue-pick note.
Chapter titles borrow documentation headings (Before you begin, Step one) for a wry voice. The ftue beat titles use "Step one/two/three"; check they read well in the player and the film.
Eyeless anchors (canopy-bath, deck/1) are not used. Garden and deck beats anchor on patio-seat or garden with the garden fallback. The ladder and the lake are in the house description and the render.
Basil (OpenClaw) works inside Docmost on the Core, not on a website, so the OpenClaw web note is not used. Imani reviews every page.
Cast gave Jonah no companion; he is a visitor with four beats. Jonah reads out the home Wi-Fi password in ftue-join; no value is shown.

Spliit shows who owes whom and moves no money. Open WebUI runs on the Core model, no cloud key. ntfy (deck-build): the script runs on her laptop, ntfy on the Core; iOS push uses a relay (catalog caveat), so nothing local is claimed.
Town Carrowmere and street Hazel Boreen are invented and still need the human map check.
